content.title: 2026 World Baseball Classic: Venezuela wake up Italy from dream run, reach first-ever final
content.text: Maikel Garcia: "Feels like we're playing in Venezuela" Maikel Garcia drove in the game-winning run with a basehit off Michael Lorenzen - who replaced starter Aaron Nola from the fifth - after Acuna Jr tied things up by beating the throw from shortstop Sam Antonacci for an infield single. Against all odds and expectations, Italy, two-thirds of the squad comprised of major leaguers, had been on a dream run as they reached the semi-finals for the first time. The Azzurri - managed by Venezuelan native Francisco Cervelli - were the only unbeaten side remaining with a 5-0 mark before Monday. The Italians took the first stab with a pair of runs in the second. JJ D’Orazio drew a bases-loaded walk before Dante Nori’s grounder plated another, putting their team in the driver's seat. But Venezuela cut into Italy’s lead in the fourth with a solo home run by Eugenio Suarez, and Jackson Chourio kick-started the seventh-inning fight-back with a single up the middle with pinch-runner Andres Gimenez on first. Daniel Palencia struck out Antonacci swinging to end the game as the crowd went into delirium. “It’s amazing. I never played in front of a crowd like this. It feels like we’re playing in Venezuela,” Garcia said.
